STAR KITSUNE 64 / CREDITS & DEVELOPMENT NOTESPROMPT 404299fcd4
A LOVE LETTER TO ARCADE FLIGHT.

SMALL TEAM. BIG SKY.

An original spiritual successor to StarFox 64.
Original characters, geometry, music and game systems.

SOURCE INFORMATION

Date: 2026-10-21 00:49 America/Vancouver.
Source: StarFox 64 (inspiration).
Tech: Three.js 0.180.0, WebGL 2, JavaScript ES2022, HTML/CSS, Web Audio API. Bundled with esbuild 0.25.12.
Art direction: Original faceted low-poly geometry, cream and mint spacecraft, copper canyons, luminous orbital machinery. Native Three.js meshes, lighting and shaders; no source game assets.
Animation: Procedural transforms, timeline events, AI steering, particle simulation and shader animation.
Environment: Codex CLI; Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS on WSL2; browser: Google Chrome 154.0.8037.57 (headless, software WebGL).
Model: OpenAI; requested gpt-6.1-sol; reasoning effort max. Runtime identity beyond runner metadata: unknown.
Testing: Two source syntax checks; seven bundle builds, with extracted embedded-script syntax validation on the final four. Seven Playwright 1.63.0 browser executions: four passed; three earlier attempts exposed two unique issues, one critical. Both issues were fixed: script embedding corrupted dollar expressions, and deferred menu focus could race rapid confirmation. Final keyboard/menu smoke and controlled-clock AI replay passed with zero runtime errors. Replay visited all three sectors, rescued Rook, upgraded lasers, destroyed the boss and looped. Physical DualSense testing: not performed.
Usage: Usage: Session time 44m 47s; tokens 3,058,195 total (2,969,716 input including 2,638,848 cached and 0 cache-write; 88,479 output including 29,107 reasoning); API cost $1.810411 USD (Estimated standard API token cost; not subscription billing).

FLIGHT DIVISION

Kite — flight lead.
Rook — veteran wingmate.
Pip — engineer, eternal optimist.
The Warden — orbital defense intelligence.

ENGINE & LICENSE

Three.js is © its contributors, under the MIT License. Included library license is retained in the bundle. Game assets are generated from original mathematical geometry. Web Audio soundscape is synthesized in real time.

ENGINE FEEDBACK

Liked most: Three.js makes geometry, materials and a moving camera easy to compose into a distinctive world.
Stuck or guessed wrong: Single-file packaging briefly corrupted minified dollar expressions; fixed with literal callback insertion and embedded-script syntax validation. Deferred menu focus was made synchronous. No renderer API blockers encountered.
Most important custom system: The complete arcade flight layer: rail-to-arena flight, enemy choreography, targeting, mission state, controller navigation and saves.
Hardest part: Keeping aiming, movement and camera language readable across two flight modes.
Remove or overhaul: Manual resource and scene-object lifecycle management.
One change: A standard input/action and mission sequencing layer for small games.

PROMPT FEEDBACK · 404299fcd4

Liked most: Clear controller-first expectations and a mandatory attract mode make the demo feel like an arcade cabinet.
Confusing: “Native art style and assets” is ambiguous for a general-purpose renderer. Interpreted as original engine-native geometry in a faceted 64-bit-era style.
Hardest: Fitting a complete, paced sortie and its supporting UX into one portable file.
One additional test: A full PS5 DualSense playthrough, including browser focus loss, reconnecting the pad and both inversion toggles.
